column1: # Game profile of Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0, no update). On the Mac it boots from the Nintendo logo through the intro text to the title screen and the attract mode (see README.md); it needs the GL layer's separate vertex format and binding

# The RomFS is empty: the NES game is inside main (the Japanese Famicom ROM, its 256 KB PRG at main+0xd721c, run by an emulator in main). SDK 10.4.0, on NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL through EGL (subsdk0, not loaded): main gets its GL functions from a glad loader

# (eglGetProcAddress, 2,956 names) and calls 45 of them, which the host's GL layer implements on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m). Its two shaders are GLSL strings in main, which dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates offline; the host finds each by the hash of its text

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)

column2: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light

column1: # load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk. subsdk0 is NVIDIA's OpenGL driver, which programs the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers main's EGL imports
# no RomFS, so no marker file
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB, a 3328 MB heap region
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
